title: Crypto-Asset Compliance Programme
summary: An advanced twelve-module programme for compliance, risk and MLRO staff at crypto-asset service providers, from authorisation and custody to market abuse, AML/CFT and wind-down.
intro: This training programme equips compliance, risk and MLRO staff at crypto-asset service providers to build, run and defend a compliance framework that meets international standards and stands up to supervisory scrutiny.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip the control functions of crypto-asset service providers and issuers with an advanced, practical command of the obligations that comprehensive crypto-asset regimes impose, from authorisation to wind-down. Participants leave able to design and evidence effective governance, custody, conduct, market integrity, financial crime and resilience controls, and to engage with supervisors the way a well-run firm should.
sections.What It Covers: International standards and comprehensive crypto-asset regimes, business models and the regulatory perimeter, authorisation, governance and internal controls, prudential resources and wind-down planning, custody and safeguarding, ICT and operational resilience, conflicts of interest and white paper disclosure, market abuse surveillance, AML/CFT and the travel rule, stablecoin issuance, and supervisory engagement and enforcement.
Intended Audience: Heads of compliance, compliance officers and compliance monitoring staff at crypto-asset service providers and issuers
Risk managers, MLROs, financial crime and internal audit professionals covering crypto-asset activities
Senior managers and legal staff responsible for authorisation, regulatory engagement and remediation
Learning Objectives: Apply FSB, IOSCO and FATF standards and the common architecture of comprehensive crypto-asset regimes to the firm's activities
Prepare a credible authorisation application and evidence real substance, governance and control
Design custody, safeguarding, prudential and wind-down arrangements that protect clients and the firm
Implement conflicts, disclosure and market abuse controls that meet conduct and market integrity expectations
Operate an effective AML/CFT, sanctions and travel rule framework and resilient ICT arrangements
Engage confidently with supervisors, manage enforcement risk and respond to crises
sections.Structure and Format: Twelve modules of about three and a half hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as an intensive multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions with pre-reading. Modules combine technical briefings with red-flag case studies, self-assessment exercises and a closing crisis simulation, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's services and jurisdictions.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Working knowledge of crypto-assets and of compliance or risk in a regulated firm is helpful; the Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals for Firms programme provides a suitable foundation.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Decentralized Finance (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Global Stablecoin Arrangements (2023)

modules.title: Crypto-Asset Markets and the Global Regulatory Framework
modules.summary: A compliance view of how blockchains, crypto-assets and their intermediaries create risk, and how international standards and comprehensive crypto-asset regimes respond to it.
objectives: Identify the real control points and failure modes in blockchain-based activities
Explain the FSB, IOSCO and FATF standards for crypto-asset activities
Map the common building blocks of comprehensive crypto-asset regimes to the firm
syllabus: Control points and failure modes: upgrades, forks, oracles, smart contracts
The ecosystem: issuers, validators, venues, custodians and end users
FSB recommendations, IOSCO policy recommendations and FATF Recommendation 15
Comprehensive crypto-asset regimes: objectives, scope and layered rulebooks

modules.title: Business Models, Perimeter and Cross-Border Operations
modules.summary: Where regulatory obligations attach across the centralised to decentralised spectrum, how they vary by service, and the compliance consequences of operating from one licence across several jurisdictions.
objectives: Map the firm's activities to regulated crypto-asset services
Identify business model red flags that attract supervisory concern
Manage home and host obligations when serving clients across borders
syllabus: The centralised to decentralised spectrum and perimeter questions
Obligations by service: trading platforms, brokers, custodians, advisers, issuers
Red flags: overlapping roles, opaque fees and fragmented group structures
Cross-border services, home and host supervisors and substance

modules.title: Preparing a Credible Authorisation Application
modules.summary: How to build an application dossier that meets the authority's completeness and quality thresholds, and to pressure-test the firm's governance and operations as a supervisor would before submission.
objectives: Build a complete application dossier and programme of operations
Evidence local substance and manage group and outsourcing dependencies
Pressure-test the business plan, customer journeys and regulatory history
syllabus: Core dossier elements: governance, suitability, policies, ICT and safeguarding
Business plans that do not outpace compliance capability
Substance, intragroup agreements and avoiding letter-box structures
Customer journeys, risk warnings and unresolved regulatory history

modules.title: Governance, Risk Management and Internal Controls
modules.summary: Building governance, risk and compliance functions that are genuinely effective rather than merely documented, and using self-assessment to find weaknesses before a supervisor does.
objectives: Design a management body, oversight functions and three lines of defence that work in practice
Operate risk appetite, compliance monitoring and internal audit with real independence
Detect governance red flags and apply proportionate remediation
syllabus: Board composition, fitness and propriety and segregation of duties
Risk appetite, risk registers and independence of control functions
Compliance monitoring plans and internal audit scope
Red flags: founder dominance, nominal independence and marginalised risk functions

modules.title: Prudential Resources, Recovery and Wind-Down Planning
modules.summary: Managing capital, liquidity and financial resilience through crypto market cycles, and preparing credible recovery and orderly wind-down plans that protect clients if the business fails.
objectives: Assess own funds and liquidity against the firm's risk profile
Identify prudential red flags and early warning indicators
Design recovery and orderly wind-down plans that return client assets
syllabus: Capital requirements, stressed positions and revenue volatility
Liquidity stress testing and contingency funding
Red flags: affiliate funding, thin capital and untested projections
Recovery options, wind-down triggers and client asset return

modules.title: Custody and Safeguarding of Client Assets
modules.summary: How crypto-asset custody works in practice, from hot and cold storage to sub-custody chains, and how the firm builds and evidences safeguarding that protects client assets in all conditions.
objectives: Assess how custody architectures affect the firm's safeguarding risk
Identify key management, reconciliation and sub-custodian risks
Design and evidence segregation, reconciliation and insolvency protection
syllabus: Hot and cold storage, hardware security modules, multi-signature and MPC
Key management, dual control and backup and recovery
Segregation, reconciliation and the ban on unauthorised use of client assets
Red flags and custody assurance: walkthroughs, audits and testing

modules.title: ICT Risk and Operational Resilience
modules.summary: Building and evidencing ICT risk management and operational resilience for the hybrid on-chain and off-chain architecture of crypto-asset firms, including cloud concentration and complex outsourcing chains.
objectives: Identify ICT and operational risks specific to crypto-asset operations
Design ICT risk management, incident reporting and resilience testing
Manage third-party and cloud dependencies with credible exit arrangements
syllabus: Key infrastructure, API dependencies and smart contract upgrade risk
ICT incident classification, reporting and internal escalation
Business continuity, penetration testing and scenario exercises
Third-party ICT contracts, concentration and exit planning

modules.title: Conflicts of Interest, Disclosure and White Papers
modules.summary: Identifying and managing the structural conflicts in multi-service crypto-asset firms, and producing white papers, marketing and client disclosures that are fair, clear and not misleading.
objectives: Identify structural conflicts in combined service models and manage them
Prepare white papers and disclosures that meet content and liability standards
Review marketing communications and customer journeys for fair treatment
syllabus: Conflicts in exchange, custody, market making and proprietary trading
White papers: content, accuracy, updates and responsibility
Marketing communications, risk warnings and complaints handling
Listing and admission policies and token due diligence

modules.title: Market Integrity and Market Abuse Surveillance
modules.summary: Preventing, detecting and reporting insider dealing and manipulation in crypto-asset markets, with surveillance systems and suspicious order reporting that work as genuine risk intelligence.
objectives: Identify inside information and insider dealing risks in the firm's activities
Detect classic and crypto-native manipulation schemes
Design surveillance, alert calibration and suspicious order reporting
syllabus: Prohibited behaviours and IOSCO market integrity expectations
Information barriers, personal account dealing and pre-clearance
Wash trading, spoofing, pump-and-dump and MEV exploitation
Surveillance design, investigation workflows and reporting quality

modules.title: AML/CFT, Sanctions and the Travel Rule
modules.summary: Assessing and controlling money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions evasion risk in crypto-asset activities, using blockchain analytics and implementing the FATF travel rule.
objectives: Assess the firm's exposure to crypto-specific financial crime typologies
Build CDD, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening and MLRO arrangements
Implement the travel rule, including for unhosted wallets and counterparty due diligence
syllabus: Typologies: mixers, privacy coins, ransomware and sanctions evasion
Blockchain analytics, wallet screening and alert management
FATF Recommendation 16 and the travel rule in practice
MLRO independence, suspicious transaction reporting and the national FIU

modules.title: Stablecoin Issuance and Reserve Management
modules.summary: The obligations and risks of issuing or distributing stablecoins, focusing on reserve quality, redemption rights, disclosure and the heightened expectations that apply to systemically significant tokens.
objectives: Distinguish stablecoin designs and their regulatory treatment
Evaluate reserve quality, liquidity and redemption resilience under stress
Design reserve, redemption and disclosure controls for an issuer
syllabus: Single-currency, multi-asset and algorithmic designs and their failure modes
Reserve composition, custody, attestation and concentration risk
Redemption rights, run dynamics and stress scenarios
FSB recommendations on global stablecoin arrangements and significance

modules.title: Supervisory Engagement, Enforcement and Crisis Readiness
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by preparing the firm for risk-based supervision, inspections and enforcement, and for managing a crisis through to recovery or orderly exit.
objectives: Prepare for and host supervisory inspections and information requests
Respond proportionately to supervisory measures and enforcement action
Lead the firm's crisis response, drawing on lessons from major failures
syllabus: How risk-based supervision allocates attention and what triggers escalation
Inspection readiness, management interviews and remediation tracking
Enforcement tools, rights of defence and lessons from major failures
Workshop: crisis simulation and the firm's compliance action plan

related.title: Digital Operational Resilience under DORA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on DORA for supervisors and financial entities: ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and TLPT, ICT third-party risk and critical provider oversight.

related.title: Fund Governance and Compliance for Managers and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund managers and service providers the practical tools to meet fund rules and supervisory expectations across the fund lifecycle.

related.title: Governance, Risk and Compliance for Market Infrastructures
related.summary: A ten-module programme for boards, managers and control functions of trading venues, CCPs, CSDs and payment systems on meeting the PFMI in governance, risk, default management and recovery.

related.title: Investment Services Compliance
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving compliance and risk staff at investment firms the tools to build, test and evidence compliance across the client journey and market activity.

related.title: Payments and E-Money Compliance
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving payment and e-money firms the practical tools to meet safeguarding, fraud, financial crime and resilience expectations.

related.title: Private Markets and Private Credit for Managers
related.summary: An eight-module advanced programme giving private markets managers and service providers the tools to manage valuation, leverage, liquidity and conflicts risks and meet supervisory expectations.
